# Introduction

This page is the map of the whole (ideal) process of data transformation for
Africa West 360 (AFWA360) project,=. The goal of AFW360 is to operationalize
microdata for its daily use by country economists and analysts through:

1. enabling access to the raw microdata as is using an API.
2. harmonizing microdata with clear harmonisation guidelines and data provenance and  enabling API-based access to it.
3. creating a reproducible pipeline of indicators creation from the harmonized microdata and enabling acces to those through an API.
4. making indicators operational for human and AI through a dashboard, data access MCP server, and AI chats.

This is a concept idea with a few developments to proof the concept.


## Where we have started

Our prior is a set of Excel files produced from the raw data. It gives an
overview of a fragment of the pipeline as well as initial version of the
dashboard developed by Moritz Meyer and published here: <https://datanalytics-int.worldbank.org/AFW360-v1/>
(requires VPN to access). Original data and dashboard code are located in the
folder `10-legacy-pipeline/`.

[Legacy Pipeline](figures/legacy-pipeline.svg){#fig-legacy-pipeline}

## Where are we going

Our goal is to create a sustainable data transformation pipeline, where data
provenance is transparent and produced indicators are machine and human
accessible and could be operationalized in the future as:

(1) statistical data
(2) API
(3) MCP server for search and extractions by the AI,
(4) basis for ai-processing and building stories based on the data.

The figure below shows the ideal pipeline: a medallion-style transformation flow,
also known as ETL (extract, transform, load). Proposed pipeline is designed to
be modular, consisting of Bronze, Silver and Gold stages.

[Ideal Pipeline](figures/ideal-pipeline.svg){#fig-ideal-pipeline}

**Bronze.** Raw microdata ingestion and operationalization through an
API-like sustainable access interface. WB has a choice of systems that come
with own strengths and limitations. The following are the main known to me:

- Development Data Hub: <https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/>. I beliese the
  that this is a best alternative out of the available because it permits hosting
  data in individual files wihtou need of deep standardisation, access to the data
  through the streamable APIs and direct integration into the data bricks and other
  data storage platforms. It is a recommended way of data publication for the analysis
  recommended by the [WB reproducibility team](https://worldbank.github.io/wb-reproducible-research-repository/guidance_note_wb.html).

- World Bank Micro Data Library: <https://microdatalib.worldbank.org/index.php/home>
  This is another alternative that is used to dissseminte micro data. The key
  limitaitons of the system is that it requires an exaustive prepareaiont of the
  metadta and data itself that brings additional costs, therefore its completness
  patchy, while data is ofen available as incomplete data set.

- DatLibWeb: <https://datalibweb2.worldbank.org/home>
  Stata native system design for GMD data hosting and deployment. I find it
  oversestrictive and outdated in the way how data is being served to the users,
  although it benefirts form the granular access controle.


**Silver.** Harmonization of microdata into a common format, with clear
documentation of the harmonization decisions and a reproducible data pipeline.
This stage establishes a shared harmonization standard across countries and
regions and enables API-based dissemination of the harmonized data. As a
dissemination platform a Development Data Hub cpould be used again, or one could
choose the World Bank Micro Data Library to share this harmonized data with a
standard documentaion in the same way as global labour database is being shared.
<https://microdatalib.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/GLD/>

**Gold.** Production of indicators in a standard SDMX format in a fully
reproducible manner that enable data access to the final users.

There are few concepts here worth exploring:

1. `SDMX` is a standard for [statistical data and metadata exchange](https://sdmx.org/). It is a
  widely used standard in the international statistical community, and it is
  supported by many statistical software packages and  visualization tools.
  It is a standard behind WDI, OECD Stats, Data 360 and other data
  dissemination platforms. It is important because it enables a transparent
  and reproducible data provenance as well as clear communicaiton of the
  computed indicators and data.

2. Access to the SDMX data by analyst is simple. Each country, surevey, year
   is reprsented as a single CSV file, with supporting metadata. Users
   simply load it into their statistical software and start working with it.
   These files could be hosted on the Micro Data Library or Development Data Hub.

3. `API` is a goldern standrad to access SDMX-based data because it establishes
   a standard interface for data reading and loading for any user: huma,
   statistical software, etc. Example of such API is data360 API
   <https://data360.worldbank.org/en/int/api>. Type
   <https://data360api.worldbank.org/data360/indicators?datasetId=WB_WDI> in the
   browser and you will get the full list of indicators available in the WDI database.

4. `MCP Server` this is a new development in the age of AI. It is a piece of
   software that local or remote AI agent have to communicate and extract data
   from the API. It is essentially needed to connect any AI agent to the
   data and metadata. In data 306 is it introduced here:
   <https://worldbank.github.io/data360-mcp/> and used across AI agents.
   It is open source and could potentially be adopted at low cost.
   The pover of the MCP servers is in the fact that they could be integrated
   into `mAI` or `k360` chats enabling data exploration augmented by
   the access to the WB knowladge and internal documentation.

5. `AI Chat` this is probably a final stage of the process, which is in
   operationalizing ai to give answers to a development quesiton based on the
   data and metadata available for the region in the SDMX format.
   One prototype is the <https://data360.worldbank.org/en/int/chat>, Anotehr
   is <https://k360.worldbankgroup.org/>.  Both use a set of `MCP servers` to
   access relevant information and leverage AI's capability to restructure the
   questions (prompt engeneering) in order to get the most relevant data and
   relevantly strucure anser

6. `Dashboards` are the human-oriented interface to the data. Having data
   structured as an SDMX database with an API enables any dashboard to be built
   on top of it and deployed through the useful chanels, e.g. PowerBI, Tableau,
   R Shiny, etc.

7. `Supporting knowladge`. This is a key element to a successful and relevant
   data pipeline. In order for AI to give relevant answers to the development
   questions that is supported by the data, it needs to know how to reason.
   This is wehere it is imporatnat to create a hiierarcy of supporting knowladge,
   including the development questions, the data and metadata, that will give AI
   correct references and templates for reasoning and exploring the data as well as
   template for populating the answer. This knowladge essentially meanst
   plain text data, which is structured and organized in a way that AI can use it:
   e.g. AI Skills.


This pipeline could be implemented in any statistical software, but its
advantage comes forward with implementation in a scalable working environment,
e.g. Databricks. We could also borrow best practices of its implementaion
from the Global Labour Database (GLD).

# Implementing AFW360 data pipeline

It is a challenge that requires commitment and investment. Yet, in the modern
age of AI and diversity of tools, this is easier than ever. The following steps
are proposed to implement the pipeline:

- Step 1: Reverse engineer Silver-Gold: convert existing Excel files into SDMX-based data
- Step 2: Micro-data harmonization and indicators computation Bronze-Silver medallions
- Step 3: APIs to the indicators data
- Step 4: Knowladge base for AI to use
- Step 5: MCP server for AFW360 data
- Step 6: Dedicated AI chat and that operationalized data and knowladge

## Implementation tracking

| Step | Short description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reverse engineer Silver–Gold stages | Planned |
| 2 | Harmonize microdata and compute indicators | Planned |
| 3 | Provide indicator APIs | Planned |
| 4 | Build an AI knowledge base | Planned |
| 5 | Build an AFW360 MCP server | Planned |
| 6 | Launch a dedicated AI chat | Planned |


##




## Step 3. Converting indicators to SDMX

**Status: today.** The R pipeline under `pipeline/` turns the indicator values into the files of the data standard:

- `data/AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>.csv`: one SDMX-CSV 2.1 data message per country and year, with a manifest. `convert_legacy.R` produces it from the Excel tables; the long table of step 2 would feed the same output through a much smaller converter.
- `metadata/`: the codelists, the data structure definition, the plans, registries, rules and surveys. This is the source of truth for what every code means.
- `geo/boundaries/`, `content/` and `assets/figures/`: the boundaries, text and figures, built by `build_geo.R` and `build_content.R`.
- `sdmx/`: generated from `metadata/` and `content/` by `build_sdmx.R`: one SDMX-ML 3.1 structure message and the SDMX-CSV 2.1 reference metadata.

`validate.R` checks every file against the standard, and `reconcile.R` compares every cell with the workbooks. The [pipeline README](https://github.com/wbEAWPV/AFW360_Glance/blob/master/pipeline/README.md) lists the commands.

## Step 4. Serving the data

Three consumers run in parallel. Each reads the SDMX files and nothing else.

- **Dashboard (today).** `index.qmd`, one section per country and an About page, rendered by Quarto. It reads through `afw360/loader.py`, the one place where the data source is wired, so switching the dashboard to the API later touches one module.
- **API (planned).** Machine access to the data and structures, for example an SDMX REST endpoint, so that other tools can pull the files rather than clone the repository.
- **MCP server (planned).** The same data and metadata exposed to AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol, so that a user can ask questions about the indicators and get answers grounded in the published files.
